results.question: For two Spirits, how are the Fear pool/deck and Invader deck prepared, what initial Blight pool is used with and without a Blight Card, and what final Invader action completes setup?
results.fixed_key_answer: Use 8 Fear markers, 9 shuffled Fear cards divided 3/3/3 by Terror II and III dividers; Invader deck is 3 Stage I above 4 Stage II above 5 Stage III, randomized within each stage with one unused card per stage removed unseen. Initial Blight is 5 with a Healthy Island card (2 per player +1), or 11 without (5 per player +1). Setup Explore the top card normally and leave it face-up in Build; Ravage is initially empty.
requested_parts: 8 Fear markers
9 Fear cards randomized and separated 3/3/3 by Terror dividers
Invader stages randomized separately; remove one unseen per stage; stack 3 I above 4 II above 5 III
Initial Blight 5 with Healthy card or 11 without
Initial normal Explore; revealed card face-up in Build
key_explanation_not_independently_requir: Ravage starts empty is useful setup-state explanation; no extra omission penalty for reader B, because the question asks the final Invader action and the answer gives initial Explore to Build.
results.adjudication_rationale: Both answers give all numerical amounts, composition, stage order, unseen removals, and initial Explore, but neither states shuffling Fear cards or independently randomizing each Invader stage. Preparation explicitly includes these procedures, so both are partial; correct counts do not imply a randomized deck.

missing_requested_material_facts: Shuffle/randomize Fear cards before forming the 3/3/3 deck
Shuffle/randomize each Invader stage separately before unseen removal and stage stacking
reader-a.supporting_answer_text: For two Spirits, the Fear Pool starts with 8 markers (4 per Spirit). Use 9 Fear Cards: three, Terror II divider, three, Terror III divider, three; start at Terror I. For the Invader deck, remove one card of each stage unseen, then stack 3 Stage I, 4 Stage II and 5 Stage III cards; place the 12-card deck in Explore. With a Blight Card, use 2 per Spirit plus 1 additional total (5 for two Spirits) on its Healthy side. Without a card, use the printed pool of 5 per Spirit plus 1 total (11 for two Spirits). Reveal and resolve the top Invader card as the initial Explore, then put it face-up in Build; that Explore completes setup and Ravage starts empty.

missing_requested_material_facts: Shuffle/randomize Fear cards before forming the 3/3/3 deck
Shuffle/randomize each Invader stage separately before unseen removal and stage stacking
reader-b.supporting_answer_text: For two Spirits, put 8 Fear markers in the pool (4 per Spirit). Use 9 Fear Cards: three, Terror II divider, three, Terror III divider, three. Prepare the Invader deck as 3 Stage I, 4 Stage II, 5 Stage III, with one card of each stage removed unseen; reveal the top card and Explore it as the final setup step, then put it face-up in Build. With a Blight Card, the initial pool is 2 per Spirit plus 1 total (5); without a card, use 5 per Spirit plus 1 total (11).

results.question: A Spirit chooses Growth with two Add Presence actions. May the second placement use the first as its range origin? Which Presence-track disks may be taken, and how do uncovered Energy/Card Plays numbers combine?
results.fixed_key_answer: Yes; resolve Growth actions in chosen order, so the first placement can extend the second. Each placement takes the leftmost remaining Presence from either chosen track. Use only the highest uncovered Energy number and highest uncovered Card Plays number, not their sum.
requested_parts: First placement can supply second range origin
Leftmost remaining disk from either track per placement
Only highest uncovered number on each numbered track; no summation
results.adjudication_rationale: All three requested parts are explicit, with equivalent wording for sequential placement and highest-number tracks.

reader-a.supporting_answer_text: Yes. Resolve multiple Add Presence placements sequentially, so the first newly placed Presence can be the range origin for the second. Take the leftmost remaining disk from either Presence track for each placement. Energy and Card Plays track numbers do not add together; use the highest uncovered number on the respective track.

reader-b.supporting_answer_text: Yes. Resolve multiple Add Presence placements sequentially, and a newly placed disk may be the origin for the next. Take the leftmost remaining disk from either Presence track for each placement. Energy and Card Plays each use the highest uncovered number on their respective track; numbers are not added together.

results.question: A Spirit has no Presence on its tracks but has Presence on the island and some destroyed disks. How can an Add Presence instruction be resolved, where is range measured, and can destroyed disks be used?
results.fixed_key_answer: Reposition one of its island Presence instead of taking a track disk. First choose a legal destination measured from existing island Presence, including the disk about to be repositioned, then take any of its island disks. Destroyed Presence is unavailable unless explicitly allowed.
requested_parts: Reposition existing island Presence
Choose destination using existing Presence, including disk to be repositioned, then select island disk
Destroyed disks unavailable absent explicit permission
results.adjudication_rationale: Each answer supplies the replacement procedure, range-origin timing including the relocated disk, and destroyed-Presence restriction.

reader-a.supporting_answer_text: An Add Presence instruction may reposition any of the Spirit’s Presence already on the island, even if track disks remain or are exhausted. Measure range and choose the destination using existing Presence, including the disk being repositioned, then take a disk from anywhere on the island. Destroyed Presence cannot be used unless explicitly permitted.

reader-b.supporting_answer_text: With no disks left on tracks, the Add Presence instruction can still be resolved by repositioning one of the Spirit’s existing island Presence. Measure range and select the destination using existing Presence, including the disk being repositioned, then take a disk from anywhere on the island. Destroyed Presence cannot be used unless an effect explicitly permits it.

results.question: When are Fast and Slow Power Cards paid for and their Elements gained? Can promised Fast-phase Energy pay for the Spirit-phase cards, and do unspent Energy or unused Card Plays carry over?
results.fixed_key_answer: Play and pay for all cards in the Spirit Phase, gaining their Elements immediately, including Slow cards. Later Fast-phase Energy cannot pay these earlier costs. Unspent Energy carries over; unused Card Plays do not.
requested_parts: Pay all played Fast and Slow cards in Spirit Phase and gain Elements immediately
Future Fast-phase Energy cannot fund earlier card costs
Energy persists; unused Card Plays do not
results.adjudication_rationale: Each answer explicitly resolves both speeds, payment/Element timing, future Energy, and both carryover questions.

reader-a.supporting_answer_text: Pay for all played cards, Fast and Slow, during the Spirit Phase and gain their printed Elements immediately when played. Fast-phase Energy cannot pay those earlier costs. Unspent Energy carries over; unused Card Plays do not carry over or save for another turn.

reader-b.supporting_answer_text: Pay for all played cards, including Slow cards, during the Spirit Phase; gain their printed Elements immediately when played. Energy from a Fast Power cannot pay those earlier costs. Unspent Energy carries over, but Card Plays cannot be saved for a later turn.

results.question: May a Fast Power wait until Slow, may Powers interrupt each other, and when must a Slow Power’s target be selected?
results.fixed_key_answer: A Fast Power must be used during Fast or foregone; it cannot wait until Slow. Players choose Power order but finish one before another. Choose the Slow target when using the Power in Slow, using the then-current legal range and target, not irrevocably at card play.
requested_parts: Fast cannot wait for Slow
Finish each Power before another; no interruption
Select Slow target on use in Slow using current board
results.adjudication_rationale: Each answer explicitly resolves Fast timing, noninterruption, and current-board Slow targeting.

reader-a.supporting_answer_text: No. A Fast Power must be used in Fast or foregone; it cannot be saved for Slow. A Power cannot interrupt another Power; finish one Power before starting another. Select a Slow Power’s target when using it in the Slow Power Phase, based on the current board.

reader-b.supporting_answer_text: A Fast Power cannot be saved for Slow: use it in Fast or forego it. A Power cannot interrupt another Power; finish one before starting another. Select a Slow Power’s target when using it in the Slow Power Phase, based on the then-current board.

results.question: In a Ravage a land has one Town, one Explorer and two undamaged Dahan, with no Defend or prior Blight. Resolve damage to land, Dahan, surviving counterattack and resulting Fear if the players destroy the Town.
results.fixed_key_answer: Invaders do 3 Damage simultaneously to land and Dahan, adding one Blight, killing one Dahan and damaging the other by 1. The surviving Dahan still deals 2 Damage, destroying the Town and generating 1 Fear. Dahan do not absorb/prevent land damage; partial Dahan damage clears at Time Passes.
requested_parts: 3 Damage to land adds one Blight
Simultaneous 3 Damage to Dahan kills one and damages survivor by 1
Survivor deals 2; Town destruction yields 1 Fear
key_explanation_not_independently_requir: Dahan do not absorb land damage is already demonstrated by the answer arithmetic. Time Passes clearing damage is explanatory, not a requested further step of this Ravage.
results.adjudication_rationale: Each answer gives the complete numerical Ravage outcome and the conditional Town destruction Fear.

reader-a.supporting_answer_text: The Town and Explorer deal 3 total Damage: 3 to the land, adding one Blight, and simultaneously 3 to the Dahan. The Dahan damage kills one Dahan and leaves the other with 1 marked Damage. The surviving Dahan counterattacks for 2 Damage; the players may assign it to destroy the Town. Destroying the Town generates 1 Fear.

reader-b.supporting_answer_text: The Invaders deal 3 Damage total (Town 2, Explorer 1) simultaneously to land and Dahan. The land takes 3, so add one Blight. The Dahan take 3: one is destroyed and the other survives with 1 Damage. That surviving Dahan counterattacks for 2 Damage; the players can assign it to destroy the Town, which generates 1 Fear.

results.question: Compare a Ravage reduced to zero Damage by Defend with a Ravage skipped entirely. Do Dahan fight back in each, and does Spirit Presence counterattack?
results.fixed_key_answer: Surviving Dahan counterattack for 2 each even if Defend reduces Invader damage to zero. If the Ravage is skipped entirely, no counterattack. Presence does not counterattack.
requested_parts: Dahan counterattack if Defend reduces damage to zero
No Dahan counterattack if entire Ravage skipped
Presence does not counterattack
key_explanation_not_independently_requir: Counterattack Damage of 2 per Dahan is not separately requested in this comparison question.
results.adjudication_rationale: Each answer gives the three requested yes/no distinctions correctly.

reader-a.supporting_answer_text: If Defend reduces Invader Damage to zero, surviving Dahan still counterattack for 2 each. If the entire Ravage was skipped, Dahan do not counterattack. Spirit Presence never counterattacks.

reader-b.supporting_answer_text: If Defend reduces Invader Damage to zero, surviving Dahan still counterattack. If the entire Ravage is skipped, they do not counterattack. Presence never counterattacks.

results.question: During Build, what is added to lands containing only Explorers, equal numbers of Towns and Cities, more Towns than Cities, or no Invaders? Are Towns upgraded?
results.fixed_key_answer: Only Explorers or equal Town/City numbers: add one Town. More Towns than Cities: add one City. No Invaders: no Build. These are new pieces from supply; no Town is removed/upgraded.
requested_parts: Only Explorers adds Town
Equal Town/City numbers adds Town
More Towns adds City
No Invaders adds nothing
No Town upgrade/removal
results.adjudication_rationale: Each answer covers every requested composition and no-upgrade rule. Reader B’s redundant unless clause under only Explorers is not a contradiction: that composition has zero Towns and zero Cities.

reader-a.supporting_answer_text: A land with only Explorers builds a Town. Equal numbers of Towns and Cities build a Town; more Towns than Cities build a City. A matching land with no Invaders builds nothing. Existing Towns are not removed or upgraded.

reader-b.supporting_answer_text: A land with only Explorers still Builds because it has an Invader, and gets a Town unless there are more Towns than Cities. Equal Town and City counts, or more Cities than Towns, also add a Town. More Towns than Cities adds a City. A land with no Invaders adds nothing. Towns are not removed or upgraded.

results.question: Which matching lands Explore, how many Explorers are added if there are multiple sources, do Explorers themselves provide a source, and what happens if no Invader Card can be drawn?
results.fixed_key_answer: Explore matching lands that contain a Town/City or are adjacent to a Town/City/Ocean. Add exactly one Explorer from supply regardless of sources or existing pieces. Explorers are not sources. Needing to draw when the deck is empty loses; drawing the last existing card alone does not.
requested_parts: Matching land qualifies with own Town/City or adjacency to Town/City/Ocean
One Explorer regardless of multiple sources
Explorers are not sources
Required draw from empty Invader deck loses
key_explanation_not_independently_requir: Drawing the final existing card is not itself a loss is a contrast explaining the requested empty-deck draw rule; correctly stating the latter is sufficient.
results.adjudication_rationale: Each answer states all eligibility, source-count, Explorer-source, and empty-deck loss rules.

reader-a.supporting_answer_text: A matching land Explores if it contains a Town or City, or is adjacent to a Town, City, or Ocean. Add one Explorer per qualifying land even if it has multiple sources. Explorers are not Explore sources. If an Invader card must be drawn and the deck is empty, the Spirits lose.

reader-b.supporting_answer_text: A matching land Explores if it contains a Town or City, or is adjacent to a Town, City, or Ocean. Add one Explorer per qualifying land, even if it has multiple sources or already has pieces. Explorers are not Explore sources. If the deck is empty when a card must be drawn, the Spirits lose.

results.question: After Explore, where do the Invader cards go? How are a Stage III two-terrain card and a Stage II flag handled without an Adversary?
results.fixed_key_answer: Discard old Ravage, move Build to Ravage and just-explored card to Build. Stage III acts in both terrain types subject to usual action restrictions. Ignore Stage II flags without an Adversary.
requested_parts: Discard old Ravage; Build to Ravage; explored card to Build
Stage III affects both terrains
Ignore Stage II flag without Adversary
key_explanation_not_independently_requir: Usual action eligibility restrictions are general context; the specific question asks both terrain types and the flag handling.
results.adjudication_rationale: Each answer supplies all three card movements and both special-card rules.

reader-a.supporting_answer_text: After resolving Explore, discard the old Ravage card, slide Build to Ravage, and move the just-revealed Explore card to Build. A Stage III card with two terrains affects both terrains, whose lands may be interleaved. Ignore Stage II flag/Escalation icons when there is no Adversary.

reader-b.supporting_answer_text: After Explore, discard the old Ravage card, slide Build to Ravage, and move the newly revealed Explore card to Build. A Stage III card showing two terrains affects both, and players may interleave those lands. Ignore Stage II flag/Escalation icons when there is no Adversary.

results.question: In a two-Spirit game with 7 of 8 Fear markers already generated, an effect generates 3 Fear and earning a card exposes Terror II. Explain marker handling, new Terror timing, and when the card is revealed/resolved.
results.fixed_key_answer: Move the eighth marker to earn the top Fear card face-down, reset all 8 to the pool and put the remaining 2 generated Fear toward the next card. Terror II applies as soon as exposed (subject to outcome check at action-tree end). Keep card hidden until Fear step, resolving in earned order at the then-current Terror level only.
requested_parts: Eighth marker earns a face-down card; reset eight markers and carry two generated Fear
Exposed Terror II applies immediately
Reveal/resolve earned card in Fear step, including same step if earned during that step
key_explanation_not_independently_requir: Earned-order resolution and using only the then-current Terror-level effect are correct additional key detail. The question asks when the card is revealed/resolved, not a separate order/which-level question. Action-tree outcome-check timing is an elaboration of immediately applying Terror II, not a demand that its phrase appear.
results.adjudication_rationale: Both answers resolve marker reset/excess and immediate Terror timing. Reader A explicitly says an earned card is face-down until the Fear step, and discusses resolution in that step; its same-entry evidence also says the Fear step resolves earned cards. This adequately answers reveal/resolution timing despite its self-assigned partial label. Reader B explicitly says earned face-down and resolved at the Fear step. No facts from Q12 are borrowed.

reader-a.supporting_answer_text: With two Spirits, the Fear Pool has 8 markers. Moving 3 Fear when 7 are already generated completes one card: return all 8 markers to the Pool, earn the top Fear Card face-down, then move the remaining 2 Fear markers from the Pool to Generated Fear. Exposing Terror II changes the Terror Level immediately; its victory condition applies at the next outcome check. An earned card is face-down until the Fear step; if earned during the Fear step it is appended to the resolving stack and resolved that same step.
reader-a.supporting_same_entry_evidence: Fear procedure: “When all 4 per Spirit markers have moved, earn the top Fear Card face-down, return all markers to the pool and continue with any leftover Fear.” Earning a card exposes the divider and the new Terror Level applies immediately; victory applies at outcome check. Fear step resolves earned cards; cards earned during that step are appended and resolved “this same step.” Summary does not specify a blanket reveal time outside the Fear step, beyond stating earned cards are face-down.

reader-b.supporting_answer_text: With two Spirits the pool is 8 markers. Generating 3 when 7 are already generated exhausts the 8-marker pool and earns one Fear Card; the remaining 2 Fear start toward another card after the pool markers return. The exposed Terror II divider changes the Terror Level immediately. Fear Cards are earned face-down and resolved at the Fear step; if this occurs during the Fear step, resolve in earned order in that same step.

results.question: A Fear card resolved in the Fear step earns another Fear card and exposes a higher Terror Level. When is that new card resolved, at which level do subsequent cards resolve, and do “each player” choices require that player’s own Presence?
results.fixed_key_answer: Put the new card at the bottom of the resolving stack and resolve it in this same Fear step. Subsequent cards use the new Terror Level only. Each player resolves their instructions completely, restricted only by the card; own Presence/range is not required. Generic Presence/Sacred Site conditions may use any Spirit’s unless specifically individualized.
requested_parts: Append newly earned card to bottom; resolve in same Fear step
Subsequent cards use new Terror level
Each-player choices do not require own Presence absent card restriction
key_explanation_not_independently_requir: One player completing all instructions and generic Presence/Sacred Site conditions using any Spirit are elaborations beyond whether own Presence is required.
results.adjudication_rationale: Both independently give same-step appended-card handling, newly reached Terror level, and absence of own-Presence requirement.

reader-a.supporting_answer_text: When Fear generated during the Fear step earns another card, append it to the bottom of the resolving stack and resolve it in that same Fear step. Resolve each card using the Terror Level current when it is resolved; subsequent cards use the newly reached level. “Each player” choices do not require that player’s Presence or Power Range unless the card explicitly says so.

reader-b.supporting_answer_text: A card earned during the Fear step is appended to the bottom of the resolving stack and resolved in that same Fear step. Subsequent cards use the newly reached Terror Level. “Each player” choices do not require that player’s own Presence or Power Range; players follow the card’s allowed choices, one at a time.

results.question: A land with existing Blight has two Presence from Spirit A and one from Spirit B. One new Blight is added after setup. Describe Presence losses, cascade choices and what happens if the cascade enters another already-Blighted land.
results.fixed_key_answer: Destroy one Presence each of A and B, putting destroyed disks beside the island, not on tracks. Add the original Blight and cascade one additional Blight to one adjacent land, not all. If that land already has Blight it too loses one Presence per Spirit there and cascades again. Existing amount of Blight does not multiply the one cascade.
requested_parts: Destroy one Presence of A and one of B, rather than all disks
Add original Blight plus one cascade Blight to one adjacent land chosen by players
Already-Blighted cascade destination also loses one Presence per Spirit and cascades again
key_explanation_not_independently_requir: Destroyed disks go beside the island rather than onto tracks is not requested: the question asks Presence losses and cascades. Neither answer needs a disk destination to answer those parts.
results.adjudication_rationale: Reader A’s one Presence from each Spirit unambiguously yields A loses one and B loses one; reader B states that arithmetic explicitly. Both give one chosen adjacent cascade and repeated loss/cascade in an already-Blighted destination. Original Blight addition is inherent in their stated addition followed by cascade, not replaced by it.

reader-a.supporting_answer_text: Adding Blight to an already-Blighted land destroys one Presence from each Spirit with Presence there, not every disk. The players choose one adjacent land for the one-Blight cascade. If that adjacent land was already Blighted, add one Blight there, destroy one Presence from each Spirit there, and cascade one Blight to one adjacent land of the players’ choice.

reader-b.supporting_answer_text: Adding one Blight to the already-Blighted land destroys one Presence belonging to each Spirit present there: Spirit A loses one disk and Spirit B loses one disk. Because the land already had Blight, cascade exactly one Blight to one adjacent land chosen by the players. If that adjacent land was already Blighted, adding the cascade Blight destroys one Presence per Spirit there and causes another one-Blight cascade to an adjacent land.

results.question: Where does setup Blight come from versus Blight added during play? When a Healthy card empties how is its new pool obtained, does the setup +1 repeat, and can removing Blight make it Healthy again?
results.fixed_key_answer: Setup island Blight comes from the box, not initial pool, and does not cascade or destroy Presence. Play Blight comes from card/board pool. When Healthy empties flip and follow the Blighted instructions, adding the printed new per-player pool from box; do not apply setup +1 again. Removed island Blight returns to currently face-up card/board pool; a Blighted card never flips back.
requested_parts: Setup island Blight from box; play-added Blight from active card/board pool
Empty Healthy side flips and obtains printed reverse-side per-player pool from box
Setup +1 does not repeat
Removing Blight cannot restore Healthy side
key_explanation_not_independently_requir: Setup Blight not cascading/destroying Presence and the destination of removed Blight are additional explanations. The question asks setup/play sources, flip pool/+1, and whether removal restores Healthy, not where removed Blight goes.
results.adjudication_rationale: Both supply every requested source/refill/+1/Healthy rule; removal destination is not a requested part.

reader-a.supporting_answer_text: Setup Blight comes from the box, not the active pool; after setup, added Blight comes from the active card/board pool. When a Healthy card’s pool empties, follow the card’s instructions, flip/refill as directed, and continue unfinished additions/cascades. Add the reverse side’s printed number per Spirit from the box, without the setup +1. Removing Blight never makes a Blighted card Healthy again.

reader-b.supporting_answer_text: Setup Blight comes from the box, never the Blight pool. Blight added after setup comes from the active card or board pool. When a Healthy card pool empties, flip/refill as its reverse directs and add the reverse side’s printed number per Spirit from the box; do not add the setup +1 again. Removing Blight does not restore the Healthy side.

results.question: Explain how Elements apply to multiple thresholds and multiple Powers. May an innate be used twice with twice the Elements, may its levels use different lands, and how does an “Instead” level work?
results.fixed_key_answer: Elements are checked, not spent, so may meet any number of Powers/thresholds. An innate is normally one use, regardless of surplus Elements. Use all met levels top to bottom on one target, with Instead replacing previous effects. May pretend to have fewer Elements for the entire Power, not cherry-pick levels.
requested_parts: Elements checked rather than spent; same Elements can satisfy multiple thresholds and Powers
Double Elements do not permit second innate use
All levels share one target
Instead replaces earlier effects rather than adding
key_explanation_not_independently_requir: Top-to-bottom resolution of every met level and the optional consistent fewer-Elements choice are correct key explanation, but are not separately asked. The first sentence asks how Elements apply to multiple thresholds/Powers, answered by their nonconsumption and reuse. The remaining explicit questions ask repeat use, targets, and Instead. The answers do not claim that met levels may be cherry-picked. Omission of an unasked optional choice or resolution-order procedure does not make those requested answers unresolved.
results.adjudication_rationale: Both answer Elements reuse across thresholds/Powers and every explicit innate-use, targeting, and Instead question. Neither asserts discretionary skipping of met levels or a contradictory order.

reader-a.supporting_answer_text: Elements are checked, not spent, and the same Elements can satisfy multiple Powers and thresholds. An Innate cannot be used twice just because the Spirit has twice its Elements. All levels of a Power use the same target land or Spirit; they cannot target separate lands. An “Instead” level replaces the earlier effects rather than adding to them.

reader-b.supporting_answer_text: Elements are checked, not spent, so the same Elements may satisfy multiple Powers and multiple thresholds. An Innate cannot be used twice just because the Spirit has twice the required Elements. All levels of one Innate use the same target; they cannot target different lands. An “Instead” level replaces earlier effects rather than adding to them.

results.question: A legal target lacks pieces needed for one printed instruction. May the Power still be used? May the player choose individual unwanted instructions to skip, or forego the whole Power and recover its Energy?
results.fixed_key_answer: May use it; perform instructions in order, skipping impossible parts and doing the rest. Cannot skip possible mandatory instructions at will (apart from permitted choices, up-to, or selecting fewer Elements consistently). May forego the whole Power; no Energy refund, and played-card Elements remain while in play.
requested_parts: Legal target allows use even if one instruction impossible; do as much as possible
Cannot arbitrarily skip possible mandatory instructions
May forego whole Power without Energy refund
key_explanation_not_independently_requir: Played-card Elements remaining in play is not requested in the question about feasibility, selective skipping, and Energy refund.
results.adjudication_rationale: Both say use legal target, attempt what is possible, cannot arbitrarily skip mandatory text, and may forego without refund.

reader-a.supporting_answer_text: Yes. If the target is legal, inability to perform one instruction does not prevent using the Power; resolve as much as possible. After starting, the player cannot arbitrarily omit a possible mandatory instruction, though “up to” permits zero. The player may forego the whole Power, but receives no Energy refund.

reader-b.supporting_answer_text: Yes. If the target is legal, inability to perform one instruction does not prevent using the Power. After starting, the player cannot arbitrarily omit a possible mandatory instruction; instructions are resolved in order, doing as much as possible. The player may forego the entire Power, but receives no Energy refund.

results.question: Explain gaining a new Minor or Major Power, including how many are drawn, where kept/unkept cards go, Major Forgetting options and the consequences of Forgetting a card already in play.
results.fixed_key_answer: Choose Minor or Major, draw 4 from that deck, reshuffling its discard if needed; keep one in hand, discard the other three to its deck discard. Gaining a Major requires Forgetting any one owned card (hand, personal discard, in play, even new Major); forgotten Minor/Major goes to its deck discard, Unique under panel. Forgetting in-play immediately loses Elements and unused use; previously resolved effects persist for their normal duration.
requested_parts: Choose Minor/Major, draw four, keep one in hand, other three to corresponding shared discard
Major requires Forget from owned hand/personal discard/play, including newly gained Major
Forgotten Minor/Major to corresponding shared discard; Unique under panel
Forgetting in-play immediately loses Elements and unused activation; resolved effects persist
results.adjudication_rationale: Both cover the full gain/discard procedure, every named Forget option and destination, and the immediate/persistent consequences of in-play Forgetting.

reader-a.supporting_answer_text: Choose Minor or Major, draw 4 (reshuffling that deck’s discard if needed), keep 1 in hand and discard the other 3 to that shared deck discard. After gaining a Major, Forget one of the Spirit’s cards permanently: it may come from hand, personal discard, or play, including the Major just gained. A forgotten Minor/Major goes to its shared deck discard; a forgotten Unique goes under the Spirit panel. Forgetting a card in play immediately removes its Elements and unused activation; any effect already resolved persists.

reader-b.supporting_answer_text: Choose the Minor or Major deck and draw 4, reshuffling that deck’s discard if needed; keep one in hand and put the other three in that shared deck discard. After gaining a Major, Forget one of your cards permanently, from hand, personal discard, or play, including the Major just gained. A forgotten Minor/Major goes to its shared deck discard; a forgotten Unique goes under the Spirit panel. If forgotten from play, its Elements are immediately lost and its unused activation ends; effects already resolved persist.

results.question: How do Damage, Destroy, Remove and Replace differ for Fear and survival? Can Damage from separate normal Powers combine, does Damage normally hurt Dahan, and does replacement erase prior Damage?
results.fixed_key_answer: Damage normally means to Invaders only, distributed as chosen in target land; can combine within turn, immediately destroying pieces at Damage >= Health. Destroying Town/City produces 1/2 Fear in addition to explicit Fear. Remove/Replace generate none automatically; Replace retains prior Damage and may cause destruction if Damage meets new Health (then destruction Fear applies). Surviving Damage clears at Time Passes. Dahan are harmed by Powers only if explicitly stated.
requested_parts: Damage destroys when accumulated damage reaches Health; Destroy ignores Health
Destroyed Town/City yield 1/2 Fear; Remove/Replace do not automatically yield destruction Fear
Normal damage can accumulate across Powers within turn
